A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DID research, with matching benchmarks and worked examples. All 12 pages of v1 and 10 pages of v2 are readable, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: Section 4 and Table 1 report original evaluations of prompting methods across three LLMs on Alice Problems, MR-GSM8K, and Holiday Puzzle.

after.justification: Section 4 retains original benchmark evaluations and adds ToT comparison results and GPT-4o token-use and cost measurements in Table 2.

M1.justification: V1 already uses progressively simplified examples, but formulates control through a hybrid inductive/deductive loss and uncertainty-dependent weighting. V2 introduces explicit complexity-controlled decomposition using Littlestone dimension and entropy. Algorithm 1 specifies N=ceil(C(p)/a) iterations and a dimension schedule from d-2 through d-1 to d, substantially changing the proposed control procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same family-relationship, mathematical/meta-reasoning, and holiday-calculation tasks using AIW, MR-GSM8K, and Holiday Puzzle. No additional domain or test scenario is evaluated. ARC appears only as prospective work in v1.

E2.justification: V2 adds ToT as an evaluated comparator for every model and task in Table 1. V1 actually evaluates only IO/CoT on Alice and Holiday Puzzle, and CoT on MR-GSM8K. This substantially broadens the central comparisons, introducing a comparator that exceeds or matches DID on MR-GSM8K.

E3.justification: The added ToT evaluations specify T=3, and Table 2 introduces GPT-4o input/output token counts and cost per case as evaluation measures. The retained experiments still use the same three LLMs, default generation parameters, 113 curated AIW problems, and 20 Holiday Puzzle examples.

E4.justification: Table 2 adds a supplementary analysis of accuracy, token usage, and monetary-cost tradeoffs across the three tasks, where v1 supplied only qualitative and asymptotic efficiency arguments. The Alice and Holiday worked examples in Figures 3–4 are retained. No component ablations or sensitivity tests are added.

E5.justification: Both versions report AIW results averaged over 20 runs. Neither supplies seeds, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests. V2 does not introduce uncertainty reporting for its added accuracy or cost results.

E6.justification: V2 adds nine ToT accuracy entries and the token/cost results in Table 2. Table 1 changes GPT-4o MR-GSM8K scores from 82.0% to 85.0% for CoT and 83.7% to 87.7% for DID, without explaining their origin. The new ToT score is 89.1%, above DID, while its reported cost is higher ($0.0194 versus $0.0128). Existing Alice and Holiday accuracy entries are unchanged.

T1.justification: V1's distribution and baseline-performance assumptions, Bayesian equations, hybrid objective, uncertainty weighting, and asymptotic complexity discussion are removed. V2 instead invokes finite-Littlestone-dimension learnability and defines H(p)=log2(product(1+|xi|)) and C(p)=dH(p), with dimension-based decomposition. This replaces the mathematical foundation, although no original theorem proof is supplied.

C1.justification: V1 emphasizes adaptive inductive/deductive prompting and accuracy improvements with limited overhead. V2's abstract and introduction add central claims of precise, theoretically grounded complexity assessment and an input-centric alternative to output exploration. They also foreground an explicit accuracy/cost advantage over ToT.

C2.justification: V2 adds mechanism explanations involving feature representations, distribution shift, information bottlenecks, and reduced output exploration. Its MR-GSM8K discussion shifts from emphasizing superiority over CoT to competitive accuracy and cost tradeoffs against the expanded baselines. Architectural and generalization limitations are largely retained and reorganized, while the fine-tuning and ARC applicability discussions are removed.

D1.justification: V2 specifies ToT's T=3 and makes zero-shot evaluation explicit across all tasks. It omits v1's clarification that the MR-GSM8K assessment portion was excluded and the past-decade provenance of Holiday Puzzle examples. These change documented reproducibility information without establishing changed data usage.

R1.justification: V2 substantially repositions DID around online-learning theory through Lu and Solomonoff, and contrasts input structuring with output exploration and recent DeepSeek-R1/o1-ioi approaches. Test-Time Training becomes stated inspiration rather than solely a future extension. Several earlier contextual references, including HoT and the cited Test-Time Training paper, disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work, methodology, and experimental narrative undergo extensive rewriting. Repeated task-specific setup paragraphs become a shared setup followed by compact results; the Discussion section is replaced by Limitations after the Conclusion. The author list also adds Serge Belongie.

P2.justification: The document changes from a single-column preprint to a two-column layout. Figure 1 gains ToT and an expanded axis explanation; Figure 2 gains a ToT panel; Table 1 gains ToT columns. Algorithm 1 and Table 2 are new displays. Figures 3–4 retain their examples but are resized and reflowed.

improvement.justification: The added ToT comparisons and Table 2 make v1's largely unsupported efficiency claims more assessable, and the MR-GSM8K discussion better acknowledges accuracy/cost tradeoffs. These gains are limited: DID costs more than CoT in Table 2, the new complexity controller lacks isolating validation, and Algorithm 1's N=ceil(C(p)/a) conflicts with N=ceil(C(p)) in its explanation. The unexplained MR-GSM8K score revisions also limit confidence.
